Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:11:1.hebrew: והא נדבה כתיבא - ובקרא דבל תאחר נמי רבינן ליה בגזירה שוה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:11:1.english: But [the law of] a voluntary offering is written - And in the verse of "You shall not delay" we also include it by means of a verbal analogy (gezeirah shavah).

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:12:1.english: [If it] died or was stolen - If he had set it aside after [the] time [had passed].

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:13:1.hebrew: משכחת לה - דאמר ולא הפריש, והויא נדבה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:13:1.english: You can find it - [A case] where he said [it] but did not set [it] aside, and it is a voluntary offering.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:13:2.hebrew: כגון דאמר הרי עלי עולה על מנת - שכשאפרישנה, לא אתחייב באחריותה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:13:2.english: For example, where he said: Behold, I [take it] upon myself to bring a burnt offering, on condition - that when I set it aside, I will not be liable for its responsibility [i.e., if it dies or is stolen, I will not be obligated to replace it].

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:15:1.english: Since it is written in the context of sacrifices - [The verse] "You shall not delay."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:16:1.hebrew: עובר בעשה - על הקרבן, דכתיב: ״ובאת שמה״, ״והבאתם״:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:16:1.english: Transgresses a positive commandment - Regarding the offering, as it is written: "And you shall come there" and "And you shall bring."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:17:1.hebrew: על ולד שלמים - שהפריש בהמה מעוברת, או עיברה לאחר הקדישה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:17:1.english: Concerning the offspring of a peace-offering - Where he set aside a pregnant animal, or it became pregnant after he consecrated it.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:18:1.hebrew: מחוסר זמן - שמא לא עברו עליו שמונה ימים:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:18:1.english: Lacking time - Perhaps eight days had not [yet] passed over it.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:1:1.hebrew: אותו מה ת"ל - בתורת כהנים תני לה, גבי פיגול: לא ירצה המקריב אותו, לא יחשב:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:1:1.english: "It" – what does the verse teach [by saying this]? - It is taught in Torat Kohanim, regarding piggul (an offering disqualified by an intention to eat it after its permitted time): "The one who offers it will not be accepted" (Leviticus 7:18), meaning it will not be credited to him.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:1.hebrew: מוצא שפתיך זו מצות עשה - דמסתמא הכי אמר קרא, מוצא שפתיך קיים:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:1.english: "That which issues from your lips" – this is a positive commandment - For, presumably, this is what the verse is saying: "That which issues from your lips," fulfill it.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:2.hebrew: תשמור זו מצות לא תעשה - שלא תאחר, כדר' אבין א"ר אילעי: כל מקום שנאמר השמר פן ואל כו' (מנחות דף צט:):
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:2.english: "Guard" – this is a negative commandment - That you not delay [fulfilling your vow], as [stated by] Rabbi Avin, who said in the name of Rabbi Ilai: Anywhere that it says "beware," "lest," or "do not," etc. (Menachot 99b).

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:3.hebrew: ועשית - על כרחך מכאן אזהרה לב"ד לכוף:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:3.english: "And you shall do" - Necessarily, from here [comes] a warning to the court to compel [him].

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:4.hebrew: לה' אלהיך - קרא יתירא הוא לדרשה, לרבות דבר שבחובה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:4.english: To the Lord your God - This verse is superfluous, [and is there] for a homiletical derivation: to include something that is an obligation.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:5.english: "With your mouth" – this is charity - He expounds the superfluous verse [i.e., the superfluous expression "with your mouth"].

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:7:1.hebrew: יקריב אותו אל פתח אהל מועד - "יקריב אותו" קרא יתירא הוא, דהא כתיב ברישיה: "יקריבנו":
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:7:1.english: He shall bring it near to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting - The words "he shall bring it near" are a superfluous verse, for it is already written at its beginning, "he shall bring it near."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 6a:8:1.english: One [case] where he said - "[It is incumbent] upon me," and he did not set it aside.

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:11:1.hebrew: איזהו נדר - משנה היא בפ"ק (משנה א') דקינין:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:11:1.english: Which is a neder (vow)? - It is a Mishnah in the first chapter (Mishnah 1) of Kinnim.

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:13:1.english: "On the condition that I will not be liable for its responsibility" - This is not like stipulating against what is written in the Torah:

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:1:1.hebrew: מדבן עזאי נפקא - בסוף פ"ב דזבחים (דף כט.) פליג ר' אלעזר אבן עזאי, ודריש דאותו בזבח הוא מדבר, ואינו מדבר בכהן. אבל רוצה ליישב כאן אליבא דבן עזאי, וכולה סוגיא מסיק התם כמו בשמעתין. וק"ק, שהרי התם דוחק ליישב מילתא דאחרים אליבא דבן עזאי. ובתמורה בסוף אלו קדשים (תמורה דף כא: ושם) גבי ר' יוסי היה אומר ג' דברים משום ג' זקנים, משמע דבן עזאי, דמוקי היקישא דמעשר לבכור (מה בכור אינו נאכל אלא לפנים מן החומה, אף מעשר אינו נאכל אלא לפנים מן החומה), לית ליה דאחרים. וקאמר: ולרבנן דמפקי ליה לטעמא אחרינא, בכור שאינו נפסל משנה לחברתה מנא להו? ומיהו אין לחוש, אם הש"ס הולך ומיישב בכל ענין:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:1:1.english: It is derived from Ben Azzai - At the end of the second chapter of Zevachim (29a), R. Elazar disagrees with Ben Azzai, and expounds that "oto" ("it") speaks of the sacrifice, and does not speak of the kohen. But [the Gemara] wants to resolve [the matter] here according to Ben Azzai, and the entire sugya there concludes as in our passage. And it is somewhat difficult, for there it is forced to resolve the view of Acherim according to Ben Azzai. And in Temurah, at the end of [the chapter] Eilu Kodashim (Temurah 21b, and there), regarding R. Yose who would say three things in the name of three elders, it implies that Ben Azzai, who establishes the analogy of the tithe to the firstborn (just as the firstborn is eaten only within the wall, so too the tithe is eaten only within the wall), does not hold like Acherim. And [the Gemara] says: "And according to the Rabbis, who derive it from a different reason, from where do they [derive that] a firstborn is not disqualified from one year to the next?" However, there is no need to be concerned if the Gemara goes on and resolves [the matter] in any manner.

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:4:1.hebrew: אא"כ מבקשים ממנו ממון ואין לו - בסוף פרק שני דזבחים (דף כט:) פי' בקונט' ממון של גזל. אבל נרא' דמיירי בנדר, כדמוכח בפרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף לב: ושם), דתניא ר' נתן אומר: בעון נדרים מתה אשתו של אדם, שנאמר: אם אין לך לשלם, למה יקח משכבך מתחתיך. והא דדריש הכא "בך חטא ולא באשתך חטא", מיירי במשלם אח"כ, אלא שעבר בבל תאחר:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:4:1.english: Unless they demand money from him and he has none - At the end of the second chapter of Zevachim (29b), Rashi explained in the Kuntres that this refers to money of robbery. But it appears that [the Gemara] is speaking of a vow, as is proven in the chapter "Bameh Madlikin" (Shabbat 32b, there), for it was taught: R. Natan says: For the sin of vows, a person's wife dies, as it is stated: "If you have nothing with which to pay, why should he take your bed from under you?" And as for that which [the Gemara] expounds here, "The sin is in you, but not in your wife," it speaks of one who pays afterward, but who transgressed "you shall not delay."

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:1.hebrew: זו מצות עשה - דכתיב: והיוצא מפיכם תעשו (במדבר ל״ב:כ״ד):
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:1.english: This is a positive commandment - As it is written: "And that which has gone out of your mouth you shall do" (Numbers 32:24).

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:2.hebrew: תשמור זו מצות לא תעשה - תימה, הא אמרינן בפ' המוצא תפילין (עירובין דף צו. ושם) גבי הא דמוקים "ושמרת את החקה הזאת" דמוקי ר"ע בפסח, דאפ"ה פסח זו מצות עשה, משום דהשמר דעשה עשה. וכן בפרק בתרא דיומא (דף פא.) גבי הא דאמר ר"ל: מפני מה לא נאמר אזהרה בעינוי? משום דלא אפשר, דהיכי ליכתוב? ופריך: ולכתוב "השמר" בעינוי! ומשני: השמר דעשה עשה. והאי נמי השמר דעשה הוא, שישלם מה שנדר ועשה "מוצא שפתיך". וי"ל דתפלין לאחר שקיעת החמה דקאי אעשה דהנחת תפלין הוי עשה, אבל "תשמור" דהכא קאי אלא תאחר דלעיל מינה, שישמור שלא יאחר. ולר' יוחנן דאמר בסוף הקומץ רבה (מנחות דף לו: ושם) גבי מניח תפלין לאחר שקיעת החמה דהשמר דעשה לאו הוא, ההיא דפסח ומילה מצות עשה ע"כ דלא כר"ע, וההיא דר"ל דיומא לא קיימי. ומיהו לא יתכן כלל לאוקמיה דלא כר"ע, דמשנה היא בפ"ק דכריתות (דף ב.), וסוגיא דשמעתא משמע בגמ' (דף ג:) דאתיא כר"ע, דקתני אוב ולא קתני ידעוני. וצריך לחלק בההיא דר' יוחנן דלא דמיא לשאר השמר דעשה:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:2.english: "Tishmor" – this is a negative commandment - This is puzzling. Don't we say in the chapter "HaMotzei Tefillin" (Eruvin 96a, there) regarding that which [the Gemara] establishes [the verse] "And you shall keep (ve-shamarta) this statute" — that R. Akiva establishes it as referring to Pesach — that even so, [the commandment of] Pesach is a positive commandment, because a "hishamer" [warning] attached to a positive commandment is [itself] a positive commandment? And likewise in the last chapter of Yoma (81a), regarding that which Resh Lakish said: Why was no warning stated regarding [the commandment of] self-affliction? Because it is not possible — for how would [the Torah] write it? And [the Gemara] asks: But let it write "hishamer" regarding self-affliction! And answers: A "hishamer" attached to a positive commandment is [only] a positive commandment. And this too is a "hishamer" attached to a positive commandment — namely, that he must pay what he vowed and fulfill "the utterance of your lips." And one can answer that [the case of] tefillin after sunset, where [the "hishamer"] refers to a positive commandment, since donning tefillin is a positive commandment [is different]; but "tishmor" here refers to "do not delay" (lo te'acher) just above it — that he should take care not to delay. But according to R. Yochanan, who said at the end of [the chapter] "HaKometz Rabbah" (Menachot 36b, there) regarding one who dons tefillin after sunset, that a "hishamer" attached to a positive commandment is a negative commandment (lav) — [the passage] about Pesach and circumcision, [which holds that they are] positive commandments, must necessarily be not like R. Akiva, and that of Resh Lakish in Yoma cannot stand. But nevertheless, it is not at all reasonable to establish it as not like R. Akiva, for it is a Mishnah in the first chapter of Keritot (2a), and the flow of the discussion in the Gemara (3b) implies that it follows R. Akiva, since it teaches "ov" but does not teach "yidoni." And it is necessary to distinguish, in that [statement] of R. Yochanan, that it is not similar to other instances of "hishamer" attached to a positive commandment.

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:3.hebrew: בפיך - זו צדקה. דכתיב: "יצא מפי צדקה" (ישעיהו מ״ה:כ״ג):
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:5:3.english: "With your mouth" - This refers to charity, as it is written: "Righteousness has gone out from My mouth" (Isaiah 45:23).

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:7:1.hebrew: יקריב אותו מלמד שכופין אותו - כל מצות עשה נמי כופין, כדאמר בפרק נערה שנתפתתה (כתובות דף מט: ושם): מכין אותו עד שתצא נפשו. והא דאיצטריך קרא הכא — משום דסלקא דעתא דאין כופין כאן, לפי שכתוב "לרצונו". וא"ת: הא דתנן פרק האומר משקלי (ערכין דף כא.): חייבי חטאות ואשמות אין ממשכנין אותן, חייבי עולות ושלמים ממשכנין אותן. ה"ד? אי מקמי דאתא לידי בל תאחר — אפי' עולות ושלמים נמי לא; ואי דעבר בבל תאחר — אפי' חטאות ואשמות נמי! וי"ל: דלעולם בשלא עבר עדיין, אלא דחזינן שהוא מתעצל להביא [ומוציא הוצאות חנם שלא לצורך, כדי שלא ישאר בידו מה לקנות], ולהכי ממשכנין; ואם אין מוצאין במה למשכנו, אז כופין, כדקאמר הכא. וא"ת: ואעולות מ"ט (לא) בעי למשכוני טפי מחטאות ואשמות? והא בפ"ק דזבחים (דף ו.) אמר דעולות נמי מכפרים אחייבי עשה! י"ל: כיון דאמרינן בעלמא (יומא דף פו.) שאם עשה תשובה לא זז משם עד שמוחלין לו, הרי בתשובה מתכפר, ולא דמי לחטאות ואשמות:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:7:1.english: "Let him offer it" — this teaches that we coerce him - We coerce [a person] regarding every positive commandment as well, as it says in the chapter "Na'arah She'nitpatetah" (Ketubot 49b, there): We beat him until his soul departs. And the reason the verse was needed here is because one might have thought that we do not coerce in this case, since it is written "of his own will." And if you ask: [Consider] that which we learned in the chapter "HaOmer Mishkali" (Arakhin 21a): Those obligated to bring sin offerings and guilt offerings are not subject to seizure of collateral; those obligated to bring burnt offerings and peace offerings are subject to seizure of collateral. What is the case? If it is before he came to [the violation of] "you shall not delay," then even [for] burnt offerings and peace offerings, [we should] not [seize] either; and if he has already transgressed "you shall not delay," then even [for] sin offerings and guilt offerings, [we should seize] as well! And one can answer: In truth it is where he has not yet transgressed, but we see that he is being lazy about bringing [the offering] [and is spending money needlessly, for no purpose, so that he will have nothing left in hand with which to buy it], and therefore we seize collateral; and if we do not find anything with which to seize collateral from him, then we coerce him, as it says here. And if you ask: And regarding burnt offerings, why do we want to seize collateral more than for sin offerings and guilt offerings? But in the first chapter of Zevachim (6a) it says that burnt offerings also atone for those who violated positive commandments! One can answer: Since we say elsewhere (Yoma 86a) that if he repents, he does not budge from there until he is forgiven, [it follows that] he is atoned for through repentance, and it is not comparable to sin offerings and guilt offerings:

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:8:1.hebrew: חד דאמר ולא אפריש - נראה לי דמשני כך: שהרי הקשה, מעשה ומלא תעשה ומעשויי נראה בכל חד רוצה ב' פסוקים, ותרי למה לי? ומשני: צריכי, בכל חד תרי קראי, דחד קרא אתא גלל אמר ולא אפריש, וקרא השני אתא גלל אפריש ולא אקריב. ופריך: מי מצית אמרת דאמר ולא אפריש? והא נדבה כתיבא ביה, ותנן כו'. פירושו כך נ"ל: היאך מוקמת העשה והלא תעשה והעשוי אנדבה דקראי דאמר ולא אפריש? הא אותן ג' עניינים, עשה ולא תעשה ועישוי, נראה דקאי לנדבה כמו לנדר, שהרי באותו קרא כתיב נדבה, כדאמר לעיל: נדבה כמשמעה. ואיך מצי היות קאי אמר ולא אפריש לנדבה? הא זה איפכא מזה, שהרי אמר ולא אפריש — אינו אומר "הרי זו", אדרבה, הוא כאומר "הרי עלי" כזה נדר, שהרי אינו מפריש אז; ונדבה פירושה היא דאמר "הרי זו" ומפריש באותה שעה, כדתנן: איזהו וכו'. ומשני: משכחת לה דאמר ולא אפריש, דמשמע נדר; משכחת לה תרתי אפי' בנדבה, כגון דאמר "הרי עלי עולה על מנת שלא אתחייב באחריותה". כשאומר "הרי עלי" הוא כמו נדר, ורוצה לעשות נדבה כשמבאר בו דין נדבה באומר דאינו חפץ להתחייב באחריותה. אלא דמשכחת לה דאמר ולא אפריש כמו האומר "הרי עלי", ועל כל זאת היא כנדבה, שהרי רוצה שלא יתחייב באחריותה כנדבה:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 6a:8:1.english: One [verse is for] one who said [it] and did not set [it] aside - It appears to me that [the Gemara] answers this way: For it had asked: [the verse's] positive commandment, its negative commandment, and its "you shall do" [clause] — it appears that each one requires two verses, and why do I need two? And it answers: They are needed; for each one there are two verses, since one verse comes for [the case of] one who said [it] and did not set [it] aside, and the second verse comes for [the case of] one who set [it] aside and did not offer [it]. And [the Gemara] asks: Can you really say [this is] one who said [it] and did not set [it] aside? But a freewill offering is written in it, and we learned in a mishnah, etc. Its explanation is thus, it seems to me: How can you establish the positive commandment, the negative commandment, and the "doing" [clause] as referring to a freewill offering, with respect to the verses of "said and did not set aside"? Those three matters — the positive commandment, the negative commandment, and the "doing" — appear to refer to a freewill offering just as to a vow, since in that very verse a freewill offering is written, as [the Gemara] said earlier: a freewill offering [is to be understood] according to its plain sense. So how can it be that "said and did not set aside" refers to a freewill offering? This is the opposite of that, since [one who] said and did not set aside does not say "This is [an offering]"; on the contrary, he is like one who says "It is incumbent upon me," which is a vow, since he is not setting [it] aside at that time. And a freewill offering means that he says "This is [an offering]" and sets it aside at that moment, as we learned: "Which is [a vow, and which is a freewill offering]?" etc. And [the Gemara] answers: You can find it where he said [it] and did not set [it] aside, which implies a vow; you can find both even with a freewill offering, for example where he said, "It is incumbent upon me to bring a burnt offering on condition that I not be liable for its responsibility." When he says "It is incumbent upon me," it is like a vow, and yet he wants to make a freewill offering when he specifies its law as that of a freewill offering, in that he says he does not wish to be liable for its responsibility. Rather, you can find that he said [it] and did not set [it] aside, like one who says "It is incumbent upon me," and despite all this it is like a freewill offering, since he wants not to be liable for its responsibility, as with a freewill offering.
